title: The parent's transport, one functor up
content: The parent entry proved the **element**-count is preserved by the k-fold Chinese Remainder isomorphism: $|\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z}| = \prod_i |\mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z}| = \prod_i n_i$. This file carries the same transport up to the **unit groups**: $|(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \prod_i |(\mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z})^\times|$. The key conceptual point is that this is *not* a second instance of the same easy counting argument. The element count reads off $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ from $n$ alone, so its multiplicativity is a triviality; the unit count $|(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \varphi(n)$ is genuinely sensitive to the factorization of $n$, so its multiplicativity has real arithmetic content and truly requires the CRT decomposition.
prerequisites: group of units of a ring

title: Reusing the parent's CRT machinery
content: The file imports `Proofs.BezoutIdentityOQ03OQ01OQ01` and opens the `BezoutCRTKFold` namespace to reuse two objects built there: the nested product type `CRTProd ns` (a right-associated $\mathbb{Z}/n_0\mathbb{Z} \times (\mathbb{Z}/n_1\mathbb{Z} \times (\cdots))$) and the explicit k-fold CRT ring isomorphism `crtKFold ns h : \mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z} \simeq+* CRTProd ns`. Nothing about the CRT isomorphism itself is re-derived; this entry only applies functors to it. The `import Mathlib` line is the gallery convention (the file is not Mathlib-bound).
mathContext: `crtKFold ns h : ZMod (ns.prod) \simeq+* CRTProd ns` is the inherited ring isomorphism.

title: Splitting the unit count of a product, factor by factor
content: `card_units_CRTProd` proves $\mathrm{Nat.card}\,(CRTProd\,ns)^\times = \prod_i \mathrm{Nat.card}\,(\mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z})^\times$ by induction on the modulus list. The **base case** uses $CRTProd\,[] = \mathrm{PUnit}$, whose unit group is a one-element subsingleton, so its `Nat.card` is $1$ (`Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique`). The **inductive step** rests on the algebraic fact that the units of a product ring factor as a product of unit groups, $(\alpha\times\beta)^\times \simeq^* \alpha^\times\times\beta^\times$ (`MulEquiv.prodUnits`); `Nat.card_prod` then splits the count and the inductive hypothesis finishes. Using `Nat.card` rather than `Fintype.card` keeps the recursion free of finiteness side conditions.

title: Applying the units functor to the CRT isomorphism
content: `card_units_preservation` is the substantive new result: $|(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \prod_i |(\mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z})^\times|$ for pairwise-coprime moduli. The whole proof is two rewrites. Because a `RingEquiv` is in particular a `MulEquiv` (`.toMulEquiv`), the units functor `Units.mapEquiv` lifts `crtKFold` directly to a group isomorphism $(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times \simeq^* (CRTProd\,ns)^\times$ — no bespoke unit-group isomorphism has to be constructed. `Nat.card_congr` transports the count along its underlying equivalence, and `card_units_CRTProd` reduces the right side to the product of factor unit counts. Notably no positivity hypothesis is needed at this stage.

title: Reading the unit count as a product of totients
content: Two theorems convert the unit-count statement into a totient statement. `natCard_units_zmod` records the bridge $\mathrm{Nat.card}\,(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times = \varphi(n)$ for $n > 0$: positivity supplies a `NeZero n` instance making $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ finite, so `Nat.card_eq_fintype_card` reduces to Mathlib's `ZMod.card_units_eq_totient`. `card_units_eq_totient_prod` then rewrites by the preservation result and replaces each factor termwise (`List.map_congr_left` under `List.prod`), yielding the headline payoff $|(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \prod_i \varphi(n_i)$. The positivity hypothesis enters only here, because $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$ has the two units $\pm 1$ while $\varphi(0) = 0$ — so the totient reading would fail at a zero modulus even though the pure unit-count statement holds.

title: What is — and is not — new here
content: Multiplicativity of $\varphi$ itself, $\varphi(\prod n_i) = \prod_i \varphi(n_i)$, is **not** a new result: it is Mathlib's `Nat.totient_mul`, and it is already proved unconditionally in the parent file as `totient_prod_pairwise_coprime`. This entry does not re-derive it. Its contribution is to exhibit the *same product* $\prod_i \varphi(n_i)$ concretely as the order of the unit group $(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times$ — i.e. as the unit-count shadow of the explicit k-fold CRT isomorphism, rather than as an abstract arithmetic identity. This is exactly Euler's own structural route to $\varphi(mn) = \varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ for coprime $m, n$.
mathContext: $\prod_i\varphi(n_i)$ realized as $|(\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z})^\times|$, not re-proving $\varphi(\prod n_i)=\prod\varphi(n_i)$.

title: Worked example: 30 = 2 · 3 · 5
content: The general theorems are specialized to the modulus list $[2, 3, 5]$, whose product is $30$. `coprime_2_3_5'` checks pairwise coprimality by kernel `decide`. `card_units_2_3_5` instantiates the preservation result, `card_units_30_eq_totient_prod` instantiates the totient payoff, and `card_units_30_eq_8` computes the numeric value $|(\mathbb{Z}/30\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \varphi(2)\cdot\varphi(3)\cdot\varphi(5) = 1\cdot 2\cdot 4 = 8$. The numeric facts are discharged by kernel `decide`, **not** `native_decide`, so they do not add `Lean.ofReduceBool` to the axiom set and the entry remains genuinely 0-axiom.
